subject: Minnesota
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Northwest Angle. 'The only place' is as the page words it: excluding surveying errors. The map shows Minnesota and the 49th-parallel border; the Angle itself is too small for the country outline.

claims.text: Excluding surveying errors, the Northwest Angle is the only place in the contiguous United States north of the 49th parallel.
The Angle is separated from the rest of Minnesota by Lake of the Woods, but shares a land border with the Canadian province of Manitoba.
The 1783 Treaty of Paris relied on the Mitchell Map, which misplaced the Mississippi's source and misdrew Lake of the Woods.
The source of the Mississippi, Lake Itasca, lies almost due south of Lake of the Woods, not to the north and west as the treaty assumed.
The 1842 Webster-Ashburton Treaty fixed the lake's northwesternmost point; the line from it cut off what is now the Northwest Angle.
The Angle had a population of 149 at the 2020 United States Census.
